raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Startup tuning can omit FlashInfer's default tactic (`-1`) and select an explicit tactic even when the default is faster for the profiling inputs. This adopts v2 candidate selection with existing v1 persistence.

## Modifications

- Import `autotune_v2` from FlashInfer and enter `autotune_v2(mode="tune", persistent_cache=False)` immediately after the existing `autotune(...)` context. Measurement policy remains unspecified.
- Retain existing v1 JSON load/save persistence, cache-disabled behavior, skip controls, streams, and distributed synchronization. Managed-store migration is excluded; upstream's existing MegaMoE integration is retained without changes.
- Add one `autotune_v2` stub to the existing upstream startup-test fixture, which already mocks the v1 tuner. No new test is added.

## Accuracy Tests

Current commit: `e4be6ffca60afd66198b53981f275b543f5ec624`, merging upstream `27b68303d043ddbddf9861c55c26bc8617ea7c35`. Relative to that upstream commit, the PR adds three production lines and one existing-fixture line. FlashInfer remains pinned to `0.7.1`.

The current merged commit has passed the local suite and repository checks below; new-head GitHub CI is pending. The following H100 results ran on the prior head `0ad44b07144da52c6af842c44b961b373afb20b0`, before merging main:

- **[H100 registered autotune suite: 11 passed, zero skips, 32.305 seconds](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/38338738008).** PyTorch `2.14.1`, FlashInfer `0.7.1`; the existing CUDA cache-persistence case and all three real two-rank Gloo tests executed.
- **[H100 FP8 model accuracy: 1 test passed, 75.477 seconds](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/38339931312).** `TestModeloptFP8.test_gsm8k`, `nvidia/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-FP8`, 200 examples, score `0.745` against the strict `> 0.70` threshold, PyTorch `2.14.1`, FlashInfer `0.7.1`. Logs confirm the startup autotune context completed and CUDA Graph capture and serving succeeded. This run does not independently establish a `-1` winner or cold/warm reuse.

The RTX 5090 validation below ran on `a9c46a964dfb87ad218d2460198848d8580bfd14` before the test-only removal and upstream merge. The historical 12-test CUDA run and pre-fix control include the subsequently removed regression.

- **Historical CUDA registered suite: 12 passed, zero skips/failures/errors, 212.267 seconds.** All 11 existing tests plus the subsequently removed regression passed, including all three real two-rank Gloo cache tests.
- **Historical pre-fix control reproduced the regression:** replacing only the v2 context with `nullcontext()` produced two expected subtest assertion failures, zero errors, in 0.439 seconds. The default-winner case selected `0` instead of `-1`; the explicit-winner control showed `-1` missing from profiling.
- **Numerical smoke through the SGLang wrapper: all six phases passed.** Real FlashInfer `bmm_fp8`, backend `cublas`, FP8 E4M3 inputs, BF16 output, `[B,M,N,K]=[1,128,64,256]`, compared with FP32 `torch.bmm` of the quantized inputs at `rtol=0.02`, `atol=0.25`.

  | Phase | Maximum absolute error |
  | --- | ---: |
  | Cold startup eager | 0.1241455078125 |
  | Bare eager after context exit | 0.1241455078125 |
  | Bare CUDA Graph replay, changed inputs | 0.0625 |
  | Warm startup through v1 load | 0.0625 |
  | Warm bare eager | 0.0625 |
  | Warm CUDA Graph replay, changed inputs | 0.0311737060546875 |

  Cold tuning made **72 profiling calls, including 8 for `-1`**, and saved **8 v1 winner entries**. Warm reuse made **0 additional profiling calls**, including bare eager execution and graph replay.

CUDA environment: native x86_64, RTX 5090 (SM120), driver 615.36, Python 3.12.3, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0, exact FlashInfer 0.7.1. SGLang Python sources were overlaid from the validated commit. The throwaway container used FlashInfer source JIT after removing its older optional 0.6.18 binary providers. Image: `lmsysorg/sglang@sha256:2dbe4c7f53230b09aaa8fa41891c13c51d9d2e253f486a70822aaf08783fff75` (amd64). The validation allocation completed with exit 0 and released its GPU.

Executed commands with `PYTHONPATH=/tmp/sglang-default-tactic-2485957-0/fi:/run/source/python`:

```bash
python3 /run/source/test/registered/unit/model_executor/runner/test_flashinfer_autotune_sync.py -v
python3 /run/source/numerical_smoke.py
```

- **Current macOS arm64 registered suite: 11 passed, 1 CUDA-only skipped, 18.861 seconds**, on Python 3.12.12, PyTorch 2.14.1, FlashInfer 0.7.1, including all real two-rank Gloo tests. Command: `PYTHONPATH=python /private/tmp/sglang-default-tactic-venv/bin/python test/registered/unit/model_executor/runner/test_flashinfer_autotune_sync.py -v` with task-local cache directories.
- **Repository checks passed:** `pre-commit run --files python/sglang/srt/model_executor/runner/flashinfer_autotune.py test/registered/unit/model_executor/runner/test_flashinfer_autotune_sync.py` (all applicable hooks, including formatting and registry checks), plus `git diff --check`.
- **[GitHub lint passed on the prior head `0ad44b0714`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/38334869160/job/115092569267).** The current merged head's lint check is pending.

Pending: GitHub CI on the current merged commit, including CUDA validation. The PR is ready for review and has the `run-ci` label. H100 unit and model-accuracy runs used the repository's PyTorch **2.14.1** pin on the prior head; the separate six-phase numerical smoke used **2.13.0**. Repeating that numerical smoke with **2.14.1** remains pending.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Serving performance remains unmeasured. Historical controlled timings and numerical-smoke profiling-call counts establish selection and cache behavior; no serving-performance improvement is claimed.
